comparator.name: Biology
comparator.sourceNotes: Current 2026 programme controls: compulsory 105 + background choice 3 + restricted RO2 6 + minimum RO3 12 + thesis 24 + open 30 = 180 EC framework. No formal major specified. Math A and first-listed laboratory RO2 are illustrative neutral choices. The minimum 12 EC RO3 block remains uninstantiated; two chair-preparing RO3 courses must also be passed, not necessarily exactly two six-credit units. Broader module assumed-knowledge wording does not expressly waive the programme condition. Current chart corroborates credit structure, not chair applicability. Registration and separate zero-credit safety/portfolio obligations preserved. Numerical 180 EC does not certify a complete pathway.

components.name: General Chemistry for the Life Sciences
The Philosophy and Ethics of Biology
Invertebrates, Algae, Fungi
components.note: Nine-credit study of invertebrates, algae and fungi combines organismal laboratory work and a field course; its two teaching periods must be completed in order. General, laboratory and fieldwork safety and the zero-credit Biology Skills Portfolio remain separate requirements. The portfolio includes annual reflection and an oral test during the thesis.

components.name: Advanced Statistics
components.note: Six-credit compulsory study of regression, analysis of variance, categorical data, non-parametric tests and statistical designs, using R. The thesis module’s Ecological Methods alternative does not remove this programme requirement.

components.name: Mathematics Applied: Introduction
components.note: Example for entry with VWO Mathematics A: functions, equations, differentiation and integration in Mathematics Applied: Introduction. Students with VWO Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead.

components.name: Practical from Gene to Protein
components.note: Illustrative restricted option for a cellular, plant or animal direction: laboratory and computational investigation of DNA, RNA and proteins, including cloning, PCR, protein analysis and enzyme kinetics. Other directions use Molecular and Evolutionary Ecology. Final specialisation and thesis preparation remain unverified.

components.name: BSc Thesis Biology
components.note: Required 24-credit laboratory, field or data-science/modelling research generating new data, with a plan, scientific article, presentations and defence. Before starting, complete at least 102 prescribed credits including all first-year credits and pass two RO3 courses preparing for the supervising chair. Their current allocation remains unverified. Registration at least one month before starting is mandatory; discuss a project at least four months beforehand.

components.name: Restricted Specialisation Study
components.note: Choose at least 12 credits from the prescribed RO3 list and pass two RO3 courses preparing for the supervising thesis chair. Some listed courses carry three credits, so the credit minimum and two-course condition must both be met. This reserved block is not a verified combination.

components.name: Open Electives or Minor
components.note: Thirty credits remain open for a minor, individual minor or elective courses.

audience.programmeDescription: Study life from cells and genes through organisms, evolution and ecosystems. Wageningen Biology combines biological theory with chemistry, physics, quantitative methods, laboratory and field research.

curriculum.routeLabel: Common programme with restricted specialisation choices
curriculum.limitation: The listed components reserve 180 credits. The minimum 12-credit RO3 block and its two chair-preparing courses have not been established as a verified combination for a supervising thesis chair. This is a supported credit framework, not a certified complete pathway.

componentNotes.y1-bioorganic: Introduces biomolecular structure, reactivity, stereochemistry, reaction mechanisms and molecular interactions through lectures, exercises and practical work.
componentNotes.y1-ecology1: Introduces ecological theories and principles through research and applications in nature management, agriculture, fisheries and environmental policy.
componentNotes.y1-ecology2: Complements Ecology I with data-generating field, greenhouse or laboratory investigations, a literature-based project proposal, reports and a presentation.
componentNotes.y1-cell: Studies plant, animal and bacterial cells, organelles, cellular organisation, differentiation and communication, with practical investigation and group discussion.
componentNotes.y1-analysis: Develops differentiation, integration and simple first-order differential equations for scientific applications.
componentNotes.y1-chem: Studies molecular interactions, energy exchange, thermodynamics, chemical equilibria, buffers and reaction kinetics in living systems.
componentNotes.y1-genetics: Develops inheritance, chromosome mapping, gene expression, genomics, gene manipulation, population genetics and complex traits.
componentNotes.y1-evolution: Studies evolutionary mechanisms within populations and species, selection, speciation, the history of life and comparative methods.
componentNotes.y1-zoology: Studies vertebrate structure and function, development and evolutionary adaptations through comparative anatomy and laboratory investigation.
componentNotes.y1-plants: Connects plant cells, tissues and whole-plant structure to development, photosynthesis, transport, growth regulation and interactions with microorganisms.
componentNotes.y1-biodiversity: Practises identification of Dutch plants and animals, diagnostic keys, field observations and biodiversity comparisons across habitats.
componentNotes.y1-linear: Applies vectors, matrices, linear systems, eigenvalues, iteration, projection and regression, including numerical software.
componentNotes.y1-stat2: Develops confidence intervals, tests of means, simple linear regression and correlation, checking model assumptions and good statistical practice.
componentNotes.y2-physics: Applies optics, mechanics, fluid flow, diffusion, heat and other physical principles to biological phenomena.
componentNotes.y2-reproduction: Studies plant reproductive strategies, flowering, fertilisation, embryogenesis, seeds and fruits, with practical investigation of structure and development.
componentNotes.y2-physiology: Connects mammalian organ systems, morphology, physiological regulation and environmental adaptation through practical work and a case study.
componentNotes.y2-modelling: Uses mathematical and computational models to turn biological hypotheses into predictions that can be investigated and tested.
componentNotes.y2-microbio: Studies the genetic, physiological, morphological and ecological diversity of microorganisms, supported by practical investigation.
componentNotes.y2-ethics: Examines how biology explains phenomena and informs social, animal, environmental and biotechnology ethics.
componentNotes.y2-development: Studies molecular mechanisms of plant and animal development, including differential gene expression, stem cells, communication and pattern formation.
componentNotes.y2-behaviour: Uses Tinbergen’s four questions to study animal behaviour, with practical data collection and analysis, study design and scientific writing.
componentNotes.y2-diversityskills: Nine-credit study of invertebrates, algae and fungi combines organismal laboratory work and a field course; its two teaching periods must be completed in order. General, laboratory and fieldwork safety and the zero-credit Biology Skills Portfolio remain separate requirements. The portfolio includes annual reflection and an oral test during the thesis.
componentNotes.y3-advancedstats: Six-credit compulsory study of regression, analysis of variance, categorical data, non-parametric tests and statistical designs, using R. The thesis module’s Ecological Methods alternative does not remove this programme requirement.
componentNotes.y1-mathchoice: Example for entry with VWO Mathematics A: functions, equations, differentiation and integration in Mathematics Applied: Introduction. Students with VWO Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead.
componentNotes.y2-specialisation: Illustrative restricted option for a cellular, plant or animal direction: laboratory and computational investigation of DNA, RNA and proteins, including cloning, PCR, protein analysis and enzyme kinetics. Other directions use Molecular and Evolutionary Ecology. Final specialisation and thesis preparation remain unverified.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: Required 24-credit laboratory, field or data-science/modelling research generating new data, with a plan, scientific article, presentations and defence. Before starting, complete at least 102 prescribed credits including all first-year credits and pass two RO3 courses preparing for the supervising chair. Their current allocation remains unverified. Registration at least one month before starting is mandatory; discuss a project at least four months beforehand.
componentNotes.y3-ro3: Choose at least 12 credits from the prescribed RO3 list and pass two RO3 courses preparing for the supervising thesis chair. Some listed courses carry three credits, so the credit minimum and two-course condition must both be met. This reserved block is not a verified combination.
componentNotes.y3-choice: Thirty credits remain open for a minor, individual minor or elective courses.
